questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Since I am studying Japanese studies it is mandatory to go on exchange in Japan, But i chose to study in the city of Fukuoka since it seemed like a nice city with lots of culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed my study abroad it gave me a lot of amazing experiences and oppurtunites.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Seinan Gakuin University was very helpful in setting you up in Japan, they had a lot of systems in place that would help you get comfortable in both your dorm and the University.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Different systems like "buddy-system" and they had tutors/managers at the dorms that would help you. Via the buddy system you would be contacted by a japanese student before arrival and they would answer any questions you had about Japan and life at Seinan. The managers and tutors were Japanese students living at the dorms that would help with going to the ward office and such.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are 3 dorms located at Seinan, HEKIHA, MINATO and MIGIWA. HEKIHA and MINATO are co-ed dorms and MIGIWA is a female only dorm.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In HEKIHA (were I lived) there was a big communal kitchen on the first floor and a smaller kitchen on every floor

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: When living in a dorm you NEED to mindful of other people and clean up after yourself, otherwise the enviroment might become less friendly and people will get annoyed and it causes unneccesary conflict.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I signed up for classes before arriving in Japan and was told whether i got them or not when i arrived in Japan. The process was pretty easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: On campus there was and international department that would help exchange students with everything they needed from paperwork to classes, which made it easy to solve your problems.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all the classes i wanted so i faced no trouble at all.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you have a backup course in mind if you dont get all the ones you wanted originally.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level of the couses might be a little lower than that of UCPH, but there was a bunch of interesting courses which definitely are worth taking and are fun.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In Japan and on Seinan the focus is more on classroom teaching and attendance then that of UCPH. You need to show up to your classes

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Comprehensive Japanese III
- Japanese reading III
- Japanese Writing III
- Japanese society and culture through manga and Anime A
- Cultural exchange between Japan and the West A
- Tandem learning II

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I highly recommend taking the Japanese society through manga and Anime if you have interest i manga or anime, since it is a super good way to learn about culture through media you already enjoy. 

I would also highly recommend that you take Tandem Learning. Tandem learning is a class where you are mixed with japanese student at make presentation based on activities you in class and out of class. It forces you to practice you japanese more which is good and its a great way to make friends with the japanese students at Seinan. Even though this class might be a little scary or intimidating at first its a class that will push your japanese ability.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is super cheap, though fruits are not, so if you are into fruits that will be a little more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't participate in any club activities during my stay but had some friends enrolled in clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a bunch of different clubs you could join a lot of sports and traditional sports clubs, buty also stuff like boardgames and music clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The university will probalby be hosting parties and events that i would recommend you join in on.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
When on kyushu i recommend grabbing a couple of friends (hopefully on of you has a drivers license) and rent a car and drive to different cities in kyushu. Rentic a car with a couple of people is cheaper than the trains and you can see a lot more "hidden stuff" like stuff you cant easily take a train to. Some locations i recommend is Oita and and theres a lot of temples in south fukuoka.

Go hiking, this was an activity i really enjoyed. Japan has lots of mountains and the views are great and the people that go hiking are typically super nice. Its also a great way to see the nature of Japan and if you are going to Fukuoka I personally recommend Aburayama mountain and Mt. Iimori (飯盛山).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I felt i was pretty easy after a week or two, i felt comfortable in Fukuoka and at Seinan

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take tandem learning, Hang out at your dorm, and go to the Seinan events

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find anything too challenging as much as it is just adjusting a bit.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciate the general kindness of Japanese culture and how mindful they are of other people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Come with an open mind. 

Dont spend all your time studying, go explore the local culture and nature.

Pack more of the stuff you consider essential because you might not be able to buy it easily in Japan. Especially painkillers, please bring your own painkillers as they are not just over the counter medicine in Japan.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
You might wanna pack more deodorant from home since the Japanese ones are quite weak (this might sound weird, but trust me).

Bring souvenirs (it can be small), the japanese really appreciate it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I think i really got a good grasp of the culture and i developed my japanese skills, and now being able to interact with more parts of the culture is very rewarding.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was my first time living "alone", of course i was living at a dorm with people around me all the time, but there was a lot of stuff for me to learn but it was worth it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Please enjoy your stay abroad.

For me it has become an unforgettable experience and i really enjoyed it. 

Some people might not like it as much but I think that is also ok, now you at least know that living abroad isn't for you.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
